id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.ic_name: ARM CoreSight On-Chip Debug and Trace Architecture
fields.topology_type: Two superimposed on-chip fabrics: a debug-access fabric (debugger -> DAP Debug Port -> Access Ports -> Debug APB / system buses -> component registers) and a trace fabric (sources -> ATB -> funnel (merge) -> replicator (fan-out) -> sinks), plus a cross-trigger channel fabric (CTIs linked by the CTM). Components are discovered through a ROM-Table hierarchy.

supported_topologies.name: Single-core debug+trace
supported_topologies.description: One DAP, one ETM, a small ATB path to one sink (e.g. ETB or TPIU).

supported_topologies.name: Multi-core SoC
supported_topologies.description: Per-core ETM/CTI; funnels merge the ATB streams; replicators fan trace to multiple sinks; CTM links all CTIs for synchronous halt/restart.

supported_topologies.name: Trace-to-DRAM
supported_topologies.description: ETR masters AXI to write a large trace buffer into system memory.

supported_topologies.name: ROM-Table hierarchy
supported_topologies.description: Nested ROM Tables describe the component layout for discovery.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Master of the debug-access fabric; reads/writes component registers via Access Ports.
Terminates trace (TPIU off-chip / ETB-ETF on-chip / ETR to DRAM).
CTIs exchange events over the CTM channel fabric.

fields.interconnect_role: CoreSight stitches a SoC's debuggable components together: the DAP gives a debugger uniform memory-mapped access to every component's registers, the ATB carries trace from many sources to one or more sinks through funnels and replicators, and the CTM lets a debug event on one component act on others (e.g. synchronous halt). The ROM-Table hierarchy makes the whole assembly self-describing.

ordering_guarantees.transaction_order: Strict sequential — each 46-bit transaction completes before the next begins. Posted reads pipeline the data return, but the wire-level ordering of transactions is strict.
ordering_guarantees.posted_read_pipelining: Read N's data appears with the ACK of transaction N+1 (or RDBUFF).
ordering_guarantees.ap_register_atomicity: Each AP register access is atomic from the host's POV.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: CoreSight debug registers are memory-mapped in a debug register space (Debug APB), 4 KB per component, located via ROM-Table offsets; system memory is reached through AHB-AP/AXI-AP. Trace is identified by ATB trace ID, not by a memory address.
